baseline.snapshot_command_timing: Executed before modifying either production file; it is a historical pre-edit check, not a command expected to pass against final production.

constraints: No GPU/provider/holdout, host PID discovery, raw signal cleanup, new runner/service/database, or commits/pushes.

contract: launch retains all A arguments and adds domain_run=None; A's seven-field action path remains the default and does not import/select a Domain.

Opt-in DomainRun is verified by the process-local strong registry against the actual persisted raw task config SHA and detached prepared action. Native captures its metadata and retains the strong run in the private owner.

Sources are strong same-Lake captures; normal-read offset-zero sealed read-only FDs are passed worker-only alongside the separate inline input FD. Full source verification stays outside writer transactions.

Natural TREE_CLOSED precedes artifact preparation and bounded strict result parsing/Domain.interpret. No observation declaration still requires explicit tuple(); declared malformed/missing output or a non-tuple never degrades into zero observations.

On failure/STOP, no Domain interpretation or scientific result is manufactured. On success, prepared artifact records and zero-to-32 v2 observation records are inserted while RUNNING, followed by lifecycle/terminal and exact-set watches in the same execution effect transaction.

watch_observations is same-task metadata-only. watch_cpu_sources is cross-task read-only and requires a strong original same-Lake/connection/scope capture; it does not relax watch_dependency/artifact ownership or grant source write authority.
Watch verification occurs immediately, before SQL commit and after SQL commit before effect confirmation. Native settles the existing budget only after the whole effect context exits.

native_module.note: The source FD case runs both a real source producer and a real evaluator. Failed first-draft CommandDomain cases stopped before prepare; the fixed cases reach their stated real CPU/READY boundaries.

watch_module.classification: Real SQLite and bounded metadata mechanisms, not OS/tree-closure evidence.

test_classification.note: These are new interface mechanisms. The draft None comparison failure and the first new-test exception mismatch are retained separately below; neither is called an old released behavior defect.

final_bounded.note: Author bounded validation only, not the actual CLI product suite, whole Core/Pro, or full V1-06 closure.

independent_review.conclusion: No blocker found in this bounded metadata contract/store scope. V1 remains the original five-field/same-subject path; V2 requires explicit version and exact input-ID producer/spec/content bindings. Nonempty observations still require result artifacts produced by their own exact evaluator ref. No source closure or scientific validity is inferred by these factories.
independent_review.independent_test_scope: The final 179 group includes the peer's 36 v2 new tests and old observation neighbors, with their source/test hashes unchanged.

peer_review_of_owned.attribution: Peer reported reading the complete native/authority diff and entire new publication module, with no new thin-layer blocker. This author does not relabel that read-only peer review as a peer test run.

limitations: Registry-selected Domain code is trusted Python, not a sandbox, import/content attestation, CPU-time bound, or provider budget.
Source capture is a process-local capability and conservative current-source fence, not restart adoption or permission to write a prior task.
The observation claims, values and comparison scope are domain declarations, not Core validation of scientific truth, statistical independence, rank or convergence.
Result reading is capped at the declared output bound and independently at 1 MiB; source aggregate/read-only FD limits belong to the separately authored source module.
Old/native handles and reservations remain HOLD after uncertain launch/publication; no new refund, retry, recovery or detached cleanup semantics are added.

The generic postcommit observation rewrite test uses real SQLite with an explicit commit wrapper and no OS claim. The native terminal-trigger test uses real CPU plus a controlled SQL trigger before commit. The report does not claim a hostile-code filesystem sandbox or coverage of every possible callback race.
No whole-suite or next V1-07/holdout completion is claimed. Root owns product/global validation and the slice closing decision.
